shafts.shaft_diameter_de.title: Shaft diameter, combined bending and torsion (DE-Goodman/Gerber/ASME)
assumptions: Solid round shaft, fully reversed or steady loading as entered (magnitudes only). Kf, Kfs are the fatigue notch factors from the geometry (user inputs, see the fatigue section). For a rotating shaft with steady torque and reversed bending, Ta = Tm = Mm = 0. The Gerber diameter is written without a 1/A factor so a steady-only load (A = 0) gives the limit d = (16 n B/(π Sut))^(1/3) instead of dividing by zero. d_elliptic needs Sy; d_goodman/d_gerber need Sut.
method_references: Distortion-energy shaft sizing: DE-Goodman, DE-Gerber and DE-ASME-elliptic diameters (recalled)

shafts.shaft_deflection_slope.title: Stepped-shaft deflection and slope (M/EI integration)

variables.name: supports
variables.desc: support positions [a, b] (m) — required only for simply_supported; for a cantilever pass [] (the value is not used)

variables.name: deflections
variables.desc: deflection [[x (m), y (m)], ...] at each load and support

variables.name: slopes
variables.desc: slope [[x (m), dy/dx (rad)], ...] at each load and support

procedure.python:
def _shaft_deflection(values):
    """Deflection and slope at loads/supports plus maxima, for a stepped shaft."""
    case = values['case']
    loads = values['loads']
    supports = values.get('supports') or [0.0, 0.0]
    sol = _beam_solution(case, values['segments'], loads, supports, values['E'])
    xg, y, slope = sol['x'], sol['y'], sol['slope']
    pts = _eval_points(case, loads, supports)
    defls = [[x, float(np.interp(x, xg, y))] for x in pts]
    slps = [[x, float(np.interp(x, xg, slope))] for x in pts]
    iy = int(np.argmax(np.abs(y)))
    isl = int(np.argmax(np.abs(slope)))
    return {'deflections': defls, 'slopes': slps, 'reactions': sol['reactions'],
            'max_deflection': abs(float(y[iy])), 'max_deflection_x': float(xg[iy]),
            'max_slope': abs(float(slope[isl])), 'max_slope_x': float(xg[isl])}

assumptions: Euler–Bernoulli beam theory, linear elastic, small deflections; point loads only. Each step is a round section I = πd⁴/64. Integration nodes are placed at every diameter step and load position, so M/(EI) is integrated exactly. Downward loads give downward (negative) y; maxima are magnitudes. Bearings at the supports, gears at the load positions. supports is required only for simply_supported (ignored for a cantilever). This calculator supplies only the static deflections/slopes; the Rayleigh/Dunkerley critical-speed relations live in the vibrations section.
method_references: Double integration of M/(EI) with support boundary conditions

shafts.shaft_critical_speed.title: Stepped-shaft first critical speed (Rayleigh)

variables.name: supports
variables.desc: support positions [a, b] (m) — required only for simply_supported; for a cantilever pass [] (the value is not used)

variables.name: deflections
variables.desc: static deflection [[x (m), y (m)], ...] at each mass

procedure.python:
def _shaft_critical_speed(values):
    """First bending critical speed of a stepped shaft by Rayleigh's method (static deflections under
    the mass weights). ω = sqrt(g·Σ m_i·δ_i / Σ m_i·δ_i²) with δ_i the deflections at the masses."""
    masses = values['masses']
    if not isinstance(masses, list) or not masses:
        raise MechError('critical_speed: masses = [[x_m, m_kg], ...]')
    weights = []
    for row in masses:
        if len(row) != 2:
            raise MechError('critical_speed: each row must be [x_m, m_kg]')
        weights.append([float(row[0]), float(row[1]) * G0])
    case = values['case']
    supports = values.get('supports') or [0.0, 0.0]
    sol = _beam_solution(case, values['segments'], weights, supports, values['E'])
    num = den = 0.0
    defls = []
    for row in masses:
        x, m = float(row[0]), float(row[1])
        y = float(np.interp(x, sol['x'], sol['y']))
        d_i = -y                      # downward-positive static deflection under the weights
        if d_i <= 0:
            raise MechError('critical_speed: a mass deflects upward; Rayleigh (weight-based) needs '
                            'downward deflections — check supports and mass positions')
        defls.append([x, y])
        num += m * d_i
        den += m * d_i * d_i
    if num <= 0 or den <= 0:
        raise MechError('critical_speed: Rayleigh numerator/denominator must be positive; check '
                        'supports and mass positions')
    return {'omega_cr': math.sqrt(G0 * num / den), 'deflections': defls}

assumptions: Rayleigh method applied to the static deflections computed by this module: ω = sqrt(g·Σ m_i δ_i / Σ m_i δ_i²) with δ_i the deflections under the weights m_i·g. Gives the first bending mode; upper bound on the exact frequency. Add gyroscopic/bearing stiffness for an accurate rotor. The Rayleigh/Dunkerley relations themselves are owned by the vibrations section; this calculator is the convenience that feeds them the stepped-shaft deflections.
method_references: Rayleigh method for the fundamental frequency of a shaft (recalled)

shafts.key_shear_crush.title: Key shear and crushing (bearing) stress
assumptions: Square parallel key; shear on the full width w over length L; crushing on half the key height (h/2) against the shaft and hub. Force at the shaft surface F = 2T/d (nominal radius; keyway depth neglected).
method_references: Key shear τ = 2T/(d·w·L); crushing σc = 4T/(d·h·L) (standard forms, recalled)

shafts.key_length.title: Key length required for shear and crushing

variables.name: L_shear
variables.desc: length required to limit shear stress

variables.name: L_crush
variables.desc: length required to limit crushing stress

assumptions: Design key length = max(L_shear, L_crush). Square parallel key, same areas as key_shear_crush; allowables are the user's material/app factors.
method_references: Key length from shear and crushing stress limits (recalled)

shafts.spline_torque.title: Spline torque capacity (bearing-pressure model)
assumptions: Approximate straight-sided/mean-radius model: torque = bearing pressure × total contact area (n·L·h) × mean radius. Real involute splines derate for unequal tooth load sharing (ANSI/AGMA); this is a first sizing estimate.
method_references: Spline torque capacity T = p·A·r_m (standard approximation, recalled)

shafts.flange_coupling.title: Flange coupling: bolt shear stress and torque capacity
assumptions: Rigid flange coupling with the bolts in shear on the pitch circle; torque = n_b·F_b·R. Preloaded friction couplings transmit torque by face friction instead (see bolted section). Single shear; use the shear area accordingly for double-shear designs.

shafts.set_screw.title: Set screw holding force and torque (friction model)

variables.name: N
variables.desc: clamping (normal) force at the cup point

variables.name: T_hold
variables.desc: holding torque against rotation on the shaft

assumptions: Friction model: the tightening torque develops a clamp N = T/(K·d) (nut factor K is a user input), and the holding force/torque follow from the cup-point friction μ. Manufacturer tabulated holding powers are more accurate for a specific screw/shaft; no tabulated values are built in.

source.derivation: Steady-only loading (Ma = Ta = 0): A = 0; B = sqrt(4·100² + 3·100²) = sqrt(70000) = 264.575 N·m. The Gerber form must not divide by zero — its limit is d = (16 n B/(π Sut))^(1/3) = (16·2·264.575/(π·800e6))^(1/3) = (3.36866e-6)^(1/3) = 14.9906 mm (equal to Goodman here). d_elliptic = (16·2·264.575/(π·600e6))^(1/3) = (4.49154e-6)^(1/3) = 16.4993 mm

Landmark: simply supported uniform shaft (I = π·0.04⁴/64 = 1.25664e-7 m⁴), centre point load. y_max = FL³/48EI = 1000/(48·200e9·1.25664e-7) = 8.28932e-4 m at x = 0.5; support slope FL²/16EI = 1000/(16·200e9·1.25664e-7) = 2.48680e-3 rad (left −, right +); reactions 500 N each.

Stepped shaft (Ø40 on 0–0.5 m, Ø30 on 0.5–1 m), simply supported at 0 and 1 m, 1 kN at 0.25 m, E = 207 GPa. Reactions: Rb = 1000·0.25/1 = 250 N, Ra = 750 N. Deflection at the load by unit-load integration y(0.25) = ∫ M·m/(EI) dx over [0,0.25]/EI1 + [0.25,0.5]/EI1 + [0.5,1]/EI2 = (562.5·0.25³/3 + 62.5·(0.75³−0.5³)/3)/EI1 + (62.5·0.5³/3)/EI2 with EI1 = 207e9·π·0.04⁴/64 = 26012.4, EI2 = 207e9·π·0.03⁴/64 = 8230.5 → −6.6680e-4 m. Max |y| = 0.993984 mm at x = 0.538687 m (slope zero, per-interval EI). Note: the review's quoted −0.6901 mm / 1.0288 mm match E = 200 GPa (a factor 207/200 = 1.035); this oracle uses the stated E = 207 GPa.

Landmark: cantilever tip load (supports ignored). y_tip = FL³/3EI = 1000/(3·200e9·1.25664e-7) = 1.32629e-2 m; tip slope FL²/2EI = 1000/(2·200e9·1.25664e-7) = 1.98944e-2 rad (downward = negative); fixed-end reaction 1000 N.
